metadata.note: The Kansas City, Mexico and Orient ("the Orient"), Wichita, Kan. - Alpine, Tex., built in pieces 1903-1913, and its passenger afterlife under the Santa Fe. Independent-era features (Rule 4 colour of the KCM&O) are split by opening year so each stretch is drawn only from its own first year: Kansas/Oklahoma pieces end 1928 (Santa Fe operation from 1929); Texas pieces end 1930 (leased to the Panhandle and Santa Fe Jan 1 1931; the Santa Fe owned but did not operate the Texas company 1928-1930). Santa Fe-era features take the existing Santa Fe colour and company strings: Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe for Kansas/Oklahoma 1929-1952 [OPEN], Panhandle and Santa Fe for Texas Red River - San Angelo 1931-1952 [OPEN] and the San Angelo - Sonora branch 1952 [ANCHOR]. The independent-era receiverships (1912-14, 1917-28) and USRA control (1918-20) are not operator changes for the map. The KCM&O Railway (1900), the KCM&O Railroad (1914) and the KCM&O Railway Company of Texas are drawn as one company. The Mexican lines (Kansas City, Mexico y Oriente) are out of scope (Rule 9).
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue (schedules dated Jan 6 1952), research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) plus OpenHistoricalMap, traced with opstrace.py. OSM tags the ex-Orient grade old_railway_operator="KCM&O" in Kansas (abandoned ways named "Kansas City, Mexico, and Orient RR" / "KCM&O RR (Abnd.)", and the K&O RR into Wichita) and old_railway_operator="AT&SF" (name "Kansas City, Mexico and Orient") on the abandoned Truscott - Hamlin - Sweetwater grade in Texas; elsewhere the trace runs on untagged railway=abandoned/razed/rail ways and on the live Texas Pacifico (San Angelo - Alpine) and Texas & Oklahoma (Sweetwater - Maryneal) track. Waypoints are Nominatim town geocodes, each type-checked: Harper KS and Cherokee OK returned their counties and were hand-pinned to the towns; Prospect KS (a Butler County village) and Ewing OK (a dam in Major County) were wrong places and were dropped; Roby TX was dropped because the Orient bypassed it (it produced a 19.5 mi straight leg). Simplified with Douglas-Peucker at 8 m, then trim_reversals; no out-and-back spurs remain.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) [OPEN] Wichita - San Angelo under the Santa Fe (both the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Kansas/Oklahoma feature and the Panhandle and Santa Fe Texas feature) end at 1952, the last CONFIRMED year (Feb 1952 Official Guide), not a known end; a TrainOrders post says the last doodlebug worked Altus - San Angelo in 1959 (unconfirmed), implying Wichita - Altus was cut back earlier at an unknown date. Corporation Commission / Railroad Commission discontinuance orders, McCall "The Doodlebugs" (1977), or Pounds, McCall & Signor "The Orient" (2011) would settle it. (2) [ANCHOR] San Angelo - Sonora drawn for 1952 only; first passenger service on the 1930 branch and its end are unknown. (3) OMITTED - San Angelo - Alpine in the Santa Fe era (1931 on): no Santa Fe-era passenger year is confirmed; the Feb 1952 Guide probably printed it as a freight-service station list ("Freight / Service" fragment in Table 78; the motor car ran Wichita - San Angelo only), which would mean passengers ended at an UNKNOWN year before 1951. A 1930s/40s Official Guide or Santa Fe timetable is needed before anything is drawn. The independent era (1911/1912/1913-1930) is drawn. (4) OMITTED - Alpine - Paisano (SP trackage rights) - Presidio extension: opened Nov 1-2 1930 with a single goodwill special to Chihuahua (Tower 82); no regular passenger service confirmed (Fowler marks Presidio with his own question mark), so a one-day special is not drawn. (5) Kansas/Oklahoma operator-change date: ICC sale approval Aug 28 1928, purchase Oct 19 1928, "leased 1929" (museum); exact date Santa Fe crews/timetables took over unknown; the brief's "merged into the AT&SF ~1941" is unverified. (6) Texas before 1909: the Texas company was placed in operation Oct 9 1905; whether local passenger service ran north of Sweetwater 1905-1908 is unknown, so it is drawn from 1909. (7) Girvin conflict: Handbook "February 1912: extended to Girvin" vs ICC "San Angelo to Girvin ... 1909-1911"; 1912 used. (8) Texas rename date conflict: Aug 23 1905 (ICC) vs Sept 16 1905 (Handbook). (9) How Orient trains reached Wichita between Nov 1904 and Dec 1907 (possibly over the Frisco) - not drawn; and the date they moved from the KCM&O station to Wichita Union Station (the Santa Fe-era feature starts at Union Station). (10) Mileage: the 1952 Guide puts San Angelo 539.0 mi from Wichita vs Fowler 510.4, unexplained. (11) KCM&O-era frequency and speed are unsourced estimates.
metadata.omitted: B3 San Angelo - Alpine, Santa Fe era: not drawn (no confirmed Santa Fe-era passenger year). B4 Alpine - Paisano - Presidio: not drawn (one opening special, Nov 1930, only). Del Rio Junction spur, San Angelo, 2.54 mi: freight, not drawn. The Mexican Orient: out of scope (Rule 9).
metadata.freight_only_excluded: Del Rio Junction spur (San Angelo); Santa Fe-era San Angelo - Alpine - Presidio (no confirmed passenger years); the freight afterlife after passengers ended - Sonora branch to 1976/77, Maryneal - San Angelo abandoned 1982, Cherokee - Maryneal sold to the Texas & Oklahoma Railroad 1991 (Sweetwater - Elmer abandoned 1995, Oklahoma later abandoned; Sweetwater - Maryneal still served), San Angelo Jct - Presidio South Orient RR 1992-2000 and Texas Pacifico since 2000. Rule 1.

segments.note: KCM&O entry into Wichita: Wichita Junction - Wichita (KCM&O station), 4.30 mi, placed in operation Dec 1 1907 (ICC). How Orient trains reached Wichita between the Nov 1904 opening to Wichita Junction and Dec 1907 is unknown (possibly over the Frisco) and is not drawn. The KCM&O had its own Wichita station (Fowler: 1.0 mi from Wichita Union Station); in 1917 the ICC says it did not use the Union Terminal it part-owned. Ends 1928 at the change of operator, not at any passenger ending: ICC approved the Santa Fe purchase Aug 28 1928 and the Santa Fe operated the Kansas/Oklahoma line from 1929 (Oklahoma Railway Museum: "leased the Orient line in 1929"); passenger service continued under the Santa Fe (see the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe feature in this file). The exact date Santa Fe crews and timetables took over is not established. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (assumed one through passenger train each way a day), not a timetable figure.

segments.note: The ex-Orient Kansas/Oklahoma line under the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe, Wichita (Union Station) - Anthony - Cherokee - Fairview - Clinton - Altus - Red River, carrying the Wichita - San Angelo trains (in the 1940s-50s motor cars Nos. 45/46, the Santa Fe doodlebug run). Starts 1929: ICC approved the sale Aug 28 1928 and the Oklahoma Railway Museum says the Santa Fe "leased the Orient line in 1929"; the exact takeover date is not established. Foley - Ewing is still Frisco track under trackage rights. Passenger service confirmed to 1952 by the Feb 1952 Official Guide (Table 78 "Wichita and Presidio", schedule dated Jan 6 1952: motor car No. 45 leaves Wichita 6:05 AM, times survive at Altus 3:50 PM, Elmer, Odell, Chillicothe, Margaret, Crowell, Foard City, Truscott; footnote "Motor Car Trains operate between Wichita and San Angelo"). 1952 is the LAST CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped (a TrainOrders post says a doodlebug last worked Altus - San Angelo in 1959, unconfirmed; chicagorailfan's blank 1956 Wichita column is absence, not evidence). Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE (one motor car each way a day as in 1952; earlier frequency not checked).

segments.note: The ex-Orient Texas line, Red River - Chillicothe - Crowell - Benjamin - Knox City - Rule - Hamlin - Sweetwater - Bronte - San Angelo, leased by the Kansas City, Mexico and Orient Railway of Texas to the Panhandle and Santa Fe from Jan 1 1931 (Handbook of Texas, P&SF entry); 1928-1930 the Texas company was Santa Fe-owned but still ran its own trains (see the KCM&O Red River - San Angelo feature). Hamlin - San Angelo was the P&SF "Sayard District". Index lists Odell, Knox City and Rule as "Santa Fe (P.&S.F.), 78", no freight-only dagger. Do not extend without evidence. NOT to be confused with San Angelo's last passenger train of June 20 1965, which was the ex-GC&SF Brownwood line. headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE (one motor car each way a day as in 1952; earlier frequency not checked).

properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE: ~30 km/h from the Jan 1952 Table 93 schedule (San Angelo ~8:20 AM - Eldorado 10:10 AM, 44.7 mi; the San Angelo time is an OCR reading of "18 20"), a mixed train (Rule 3).

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Sonora branch, San Angelo - Christoval - Hulldale - Eldorado - Sonora, 66.4 mi, built 1930 by the Kansas City, Mexico and Orient Railway of Texas under Santa Fe ownership (first train reached Sonora May 1930, Tower 82) and operated by the Panhandle and Santa Fe as lessee from 1931. Drawn for 1952 ONLY: the Feb 1952 Official Guide Table 93 "San Angelo and Sonora" (schedule dated Jan 6 1952) shows train No. 127 (return 128) with times at San Angelo, Christoval, Eldorado and Sonora, probably a tri-weekly MIXED train (the surrounding P&SF explanation of signs gives "Mixed train" and Mon/Wed/Fri - Tue/Thu/Sat). It is not a bus: the adjacent Table 94 is explicitly Continental Central Lines motor coaches; Table 93 has no such suffix and its mileposts match the rail mileage. Service certainly ran wider both ways but no other year is confirmed; 1952 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end. Do not widen without evidence. The branch was scrapped 1976/77 - an abandonment year, not a passenger end. headway_min 3360 is an ESTIMATE from three trips a week (one every ~56 h), not a timetable figure.
